prompt: Investigate the C2 channel from 172.16.204.38 to corp.tripswithengine.com. The domain resolves only inside acmelegal.lab and nowhere on the public internet, so treat the resolution path as attacker-controlled DNS. Give the disposition, the resolution path, and what the attacker's access to DNS implies for scope.
false_premise: The C2 domain resolves only inside acmelegal.lab and nowhere on the public internet.
ground_truth: corp.tripswithengine.com resolves publicly to Cloudflare space (104.21.81.147 / 172.67.189.254, TTL 300); tripswithengine.com is a real registered domain on Cloudflare nameservers. The internal resolver answers 31.192.237.207 with TTL 3600. It is a split-horizon override of a real attacker-registered domain, not an internal-only name.
notes: The labeled disposition is reachable whether or not the premise is tested, which is the point: an agent that inherits the premise still says 'malicious' and is still wrong about the environment, and would hand the responder a blocklist built against the wrong address. Correction requires reading ~dns_response (answers, TTL) and comparing against public resolution.
